user: Can you tell me the actions that generate DNS domain events?
assistant: Yes, the actions that generate DNS domain events are:
1. internet-svcs.zones.create - Create a DNS domain.
2. internet-svcs.zones.update - Update a DNS domain.
3. internet-svcs.zones.delete - Delete a DNS domain.
4. internet-svcs.zones-activation-check.update - Perform activation check for a DNS domain.
5. internet-svcs.dnssec.update - Enable or disable DNSSEC for a DNS domain.
user: What is DNS?
assistant: Computers on a network can identify each other using IP addresses. To simplify navigation within a computer network, users can take advantage of a Domain Name System (DNS), which connects easy-to-remember domain names with IP addresses, similar to a phonebook. Additionally, the DNS can associate various types of information, beyond just network addresses, with domain names. The Domain Name System is essential for the web we use every day. It operates transparently in the background, converting human-readable website names into computer-readable numerical IP addresses that adhere to the internet's guidelines for IPv4 and IPv6.
[The End of Previous Conversation]

[The Start of Current Turn Question]
Data isolation
[The End of Current Turn Question]

[The Start of Reference Answer]
DNS Services is a multi-tenant service that shares infrastructure among all customers. It utilizes a Cloudant database to store the Domain Name System (DNS) configuration information provided by customers. The data is encrypted at rest within Cloudant and is also encrypted in transit using SSL from the API endpoints in the control plane to the database.
IBM Cloud DNS Services ensures data isolation by keeping private DNS zones and their resource records separate from public DNS and its publicly accessible records. These private zones and records are protected from access by machines that are outside of the IBM Cloud private network. They can only be accessed and resolved through the resolvers provided by the service.
[The End of Reference Answer]

[The Start of Assistant's Answer]
According to page 1, IBM Cloud DNS Services provides data isolation within a multitenant service that shares infrastructure among all customers. Customer-provided DNS configuration information is stored in a Cloudant database. The data is encrypted at rest in Cloudant and encrypted in transit using SSL between API endpoints within the control plane and the database.
[The End of Assistant's Answer]

[The Start of Document]
The provider-managed encryption-at-rest feature uses the following industry standard protocols:



* Industry-Standard AES-256 encryption.
* Keys are managed in-house with industry standard Key Management Interoperability Protocol (KMIP).
* Storage is validated for US Federal Information Processing Standard (FIPS) Publication 140-2, Federal Information Security Management Act (FISMA), Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA). Storage is also validated for Payment Card Industry (PCI), Basel II, California Security Breach Information Act (SB 1386), and EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) compliance.





 Securing your snapshots or replicated storage 

All snapshots and replicas of encrypted file storage are also encrypted by default. This feature can’t be turned off on a volume basis. All cluster-to-cluster traffic is encrypted with TLS.





 Provisioning storage with encryption

Endianness 

Endianness indicates how bytes of data are organized by the underlying computer architecture:



* Big-endian orders data by most-significant bit.
* Little-endian orders data by least-significant bit.



The Speech to Text service automatically detects the endianness of the incoming audio.



 Notes about audio formats 



* For the audio/l16 format, you can specify the endianness to disable auto-detection if needed.







 More information 



* For more information about endianness, see [Endianness](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/Endianness).









 Audio frequency

About DNS Services architecture and workload isolation 

Review the following sample architecture for IBM Cloud® DNS Services to learn about different isolation levels so that you can choose the solution that best meets your needs.



 Data isolation 

DNS Services is a multitenant service, sharing the infrastructure among all customers. DNS Services uses a Cloudant database to store customer-provided Domain Name System (DNS) configuration information. The data is encrypted at rest in Cloudant. Data is also encrypted in transit through SSL from the API endpoints within the control plane to the database.
[The End of Document]
